summary: Describes the URLAUTH extension to IMAP, which lets a client use URLs carrying authorization to get limited message data from an IMAP server. A server shows support with the capability name URLAUTH. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: A special pass-link that lets someone fetch just one item from your mailbox without giving them your whole password.

questions: how do authorized imap urls work
what is the imap genurlauth command
how to revoke an imap url
subtitle: IMAP URLs that carry their own authorization, so a client can hand out access to one message or part.

tldr.problem: The IMAP URL scheme only supports authentication as a named user, so a URL can be resolved only by the mailbox owner and cannot safely grant access to a single message.
tldr.mechanism: URLAUTH appends an access identifier, a mechanism name and a token made with a secret mailbox access key to the URL, and the new GENURLAUTH, URLFETCH and RESETKEY commands create, redeem and revoke these URLs.
tldr.outcome: A URL grants access to only the message or part it addresses, can be restricted to certain users and can expire. The RFC was later updated by RFC 5092 and RFC 5550.

today: RFC 4467 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3501 and has been updated by RFC 5092 and RFC 5550. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why IMAP URLs Needed Authorization
sections.content:
In the IMAP URL scheme, a URL such as imap://fred@example.com/INBOX/;uid=20 requires authorization as the user fred. That mixes up authentication and authorization, so only the mailbox owner can resolve it. RFC 4467 defines the URLAUTH extension to IMAP and the IMAP URL scheme, which carries authorization in the URL string itself.

The RFC compares a URLAUTH-authorized URL to a "pawn ticket": it carries no authentication information and can be redeemed by whoever presents it. Unlike a pawn ticket, it has optional limits. A URL can be usable by anonymous holders, any authenticated user, one specific authenticated user, or only a message submission service acting for a specific user. It can also expire.

One use is the BURL command in message submission, which lets a client with limited resources forward or resend a message without fetching its data first. A server shows support with the capability name URLAUTH.
sections.eli5: Normally only the owner can open the mailbox. This makes a special link that opens just one message, for whoever you give it to.

sections.title: Access Key, Mechanism and Token
sections.content:
The URLAUTH part of a URL has an authorized access identifier, an authorization mechanism name and an authorization token. The token is generated from the URL, the access identifier, the mechanism name and a mailbox access key.

The mailbox access key is a random string with at least 128 bits of entropy, generated by software and unpredictable. Each user has a table of keys, one per mailbox, so two users sharing a mailbox have different keys. A client can ask the server for a new key, which revokes every URL made with the old one, but cannot choose a key itself.

The only mechanism defined is INTERNAL, where the server picks the token algorithm and never reveals the key. The RFC recommends a modern HMAC such as HMAC-SHA1, and advises that servers identify the algorithm inside the token so it can be changed later. The token is at least 128 bits, written as at least 32 hexadecimal digits.
sections.eli5: The server keeps a secret stamp for each mailbox. The link is stamped with it, and only the server can check the stamp is real.

sections.title: The URLAUTH URL Syntax
sections.content:
IMAP URLs that point to a specific message or message part may gain ;EXPIRE=<datetime> and ;URLAUTH=<access>:<mech>:<token>. The URLAUTH part MUST be at the end. It MUST NOT be used with URLs for a whole server, a list of mailboxes, a whole mailbox or search results. After the expiry time, servers MUST reject the URL.

The access identifier sets who may use the URL.

  • submit+userid: only a message submission entity acting for that user.
  • user+userid: only sessions logged in as that user.
  • authuser: any authorized user of the server, but not anonymous sessions.
  • anonymous: any session, including anonymous ones.

The RFC warns that authuser and anonymous lack the protection of the first two, since a snooper could reuse the URL. They should be used with caution, and only for content that may be disclosed to any authorized user, or to anyone.
sections.eli5: You can write on the ticket who may use it: just one person, any member, or anyone at all. You can also give it an end date.

sections.title: Generating and Validating URLs
sections.content:
To generate a URL, the server builds an initial URL ending in ;URLAUTH=<access>, computes the token over it with the secret key, and appends :, the mechanism name, : and the hexadecimal token. Hexadecimal is used instead of BASE64 because BASE64 padding with = would be a problem in a URL.

To validate, the server strips :<mech>:<token> to get a "rump URL" and finds the mailbox. It recomputes the token and succeeds only if it matches. Nothing else may be done to the URL: no percent-decoding and no case-folding.

If the mailbox cannot be identified, the server still computes a token with a random plausible key before failing, so that response time does not reveal which mailboxes exist.
sections.eli5: To check a ticket, the server redoes the stamp itself and sees whether it matches. It takes the same time even for a mailbox that does not exist, so nobody can guess names.

sections.title: RESETKEY, GENURLAUTH and URLFETCH
sections.content:
RESETKEY with a mailbox name makes a new access key for that mailbox, revoking its existing URLs. With no arguments it removes all the user's keys, revoking everything. GENURLAUTH takes URLs with a mechanism and returns URLAUTH-authorized versions. The URL must name an existing mailbox, a valid owner userid and a valid access identifier, otherwise the server returns BAD. A key is created automatically on first use.

URLFETCH returns the data for URLs. It works whether or not the session could otherwise open the mailbox, and no mailbox needs to be selected. It runs with the access of the userid in the URL's server component, so the URLAUTH itself grants nothing beyond what that user can access, which may have changed since the URL was made. Invalid URLs, and URLs for whole servers or mailboxes, give NIL.

The URLMECH status code lists mechanism names and is returned for RESETKEY, SELECT and EXAMINE.
sections.eli5: One command makes a ticket, one redeems it, and one throws away the secret stamp so all old tickets stop working.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The mailbox access key SHOULD have at least 128 bits of entropy and MUST be unpredictable. The URLMECH code may expose sensitive data for mechanisms other than INTERNAL, so a server MUST support a configuration that withholds it unless the session is protected, for example by a TLS or SASL security layer with confidentiality.

A server MAY add progressively longer delays after repeated failed validations to limit computational denial-of-service attacks. A server SHOULD only allow generating a URL for another user's server component when the logged-in user is authorized as equivalent to that user or can access their key table.

For GENURLAUTH with an invalid userid, a server MAY return OK with a key that always fails validation, so attackers cannot test which userids exist.
sections.eli5: Keep the stamp secret and unguessable, and slow down anyone who keeps trying fake tickets.

data.title: Generating a URLAUTH URL
data.code:
C: a777 GENURLAUTH "imap://joe@example.com/INBOX/;uid=20/
   ;section=1.2;urlauth=submit+fred" INTERNAL
S: * GENURLAUTH "imap://joe@example.com/INBOX/;uid=20/;section=1.2
   ;urlauth=submit+fred:internal:91354a473744909de610943775f92038"
S: a777 OK GENURLAUTH completed
